extracted.intended_audience: authors, copyeditors, typesetters, indexers, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, editing, and citing book- and journal‑length manuscripts (capitalization, titles, citations, typography, manuscript submission and production). Intended to standardize style, punctuation, and bibliographic treatment across scholarly and trade publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic rule and exceptions for capitalization; “down style” guidance; sentence-style vs headline-style; capitalization of titles, offices, works, non-English works, religious terms, and special cases (e.g., popes, sovereigns, academic titles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections 8.19–8.33 for basic rule and exceptions; 8.1 for “down style”; 8.157–8.162 and 15.38 for sentence‑ versus headline‑style; non‑English works: 11.6, 14.98, 15.6; specific cases (academic titles, honorifics, civil/military titles) cited in 8.19–8.36.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of works — capitalization and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: How to capitalize and format titles and subtitles of works (books, articles, exhibitions, art, music, blogs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalization: 8.157–162; headline‑style: 8.159–160; sentence‑style: 8.158; subtitles and parts: 8.158–164, 14.87–91; non‑English works: 11.8–11.10, 14.98–99; examples include artworks (8.57), musical works (8.193–97), periodicals (8.168), and web content (8.191–92, 14.206–08). See also punctuation rules for titles (colons, commas, question/exclamation marks) in 8.164–65 and 14.89–96.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics and quotation marks for titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Which kinds of titles are italicized versus put in quotation marks in running text and bibliographies (books vs. chapters, articles, poems, short works).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italics for books, journals, long poems, movies, standards, vessels, videogames, etc. (8.2, 8.163–196, 14.86, 14.259); quotation marks for chapters, journal articles, poems, website sections and blog posts (14.21, 14.23, 8.163, 14.86, 14.206–08). See 14.20–21 for bibliographies and 14.33 for shortened citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of works in source citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of titles of works specifically within source citations (bibliographies, notes, shortened citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance in 14.85–99 covering capitalization (14.87–91), italics/quotation marks (14.86–99), abbreviations (14.59–60), permissable changes in citations (8.165, 14.88, 14.91), and examples/variations by reference system (15.9). See also note vs author‑date distinctions (14.20–21; 15.4–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible changes to titles when citing
rubrics_metrics.description: What, if any, changes to a work’s title are acceptable in a citation (shortening, inclusive years, double titles, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible changes discussed at 8.165, 8.167, 11.7, 14.88, 14.91; handling of inclusive years (9.64); double titles connected by “or” (8.167, 14.91); shortening and shortened citations (8.168, 13.58, 14.32–33). Cross‑check titles (2.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: How punctuation (colons, commas, semicolons, question/exclamation marks, quotation marks) interacts with titles and their citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colons: 1.19, 8.164–65, 14.89–91; commas and semicolons: 6.17, 8.165–167; exclamation/question marks: 6.124–126, 14.92, 14.96; quotations in titles: 8.162, 14.94; treatment in relation to surrounding text: 6.41, 8.166.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles within titles and subtitles
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle a title that contains another title (reverse italics, quotation marks, punctuation, capitalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles within titles: 8.173, 14.94; reverse italics guidance (14.95); punctuation and capitalization rules apply as in main title sections; see also 8.162 for quotations in titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page content and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Required and optional elements on a title page: author names, authors/editors/translators’ names, edition number, place and date of publication, publishers’ names, distribution information, foreword/author of foreword, multiauthor volume considerations, and pagination/running head rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title page guidance: 1.17–1.19; authors’/editors’/translators’ names: 1.19, 14.73, 14.82, 14.101, 15.12; edition number: 1.19, 1.26, 14.113; place and publication date: 1.19, 14.129, 14.142; publishers’ names: 1.19, 14.129, 14.133; running heads omitted (1.11); pagination omitted on title page (1.7); submission and editing notes: 2.3, 2.57.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citations — notes and bibliography vs author‑date systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in abbreviation, capitalization, order, and formatting between notes & bibliography and author‑date reference systems, including examples and variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes & bibliography: abbreviations and order: 14.59–60, 14.71, 14.79; capitalization and examples: 14.20–21, 14.23, 14.86–107; author‑date: abbreviations, capitalization and examples: 15.4–15.13; see examples and cross‑references in 15.9 and fig. 14.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal‑style citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Special citation forms and treatments for legal and public documents: cases, legislation, treaties, hearings, parliamentary materials, international entities, and U.S. congressional materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See legal‑style guidance in 14.270–305 covering cases (14.272, 14.276), legislation (14.295, 14.300), treaties (14.290), hearings (14.284), legislative debates (14.286–87), parliamentary publications (14.299–303), and resources on specific jurisdictions (e.g., UK: 14.297–303; US: 14.282–292).

rubrics_metrics.name: URLs and DOIs in citations and text
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how to include URLs, DOI‑based URLs, permalinks, short forms, line‑breaking behavior, and access/revision dates in citations and text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined and recommended uses: 14.6, 14.9–18, 14.161; DOI‑based URLs: 1.33, 1.79, 14.8; permalinks and short forms: 14.9–10, 14.15; line breaks and punctuation with URLs: 2.13, 6.113, 7.46, 14.17–18; access/revision dates: 14.12, 14.13, 14.207; recommended use in citations for many types of material (14.161–187, § by material type).

rubrics_metrics.name: URLs as website identifiers and web content citation
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat website titles, lack of formal titles, owner/sponsor identification, revision dates, author attribution, and copyright when citing web pages and web content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance in 14.205–14.210 and 8.191: identify sites with no formal title (8.191); owner/sponsor: 14.14, 14.207, 14.267; revision dates: 14.13; preprints and publisher websites: 1.113, 1.121; social media content: 14.206–209; permissions processing via websites: 4.97.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished and informally published materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition, treatment in citation, permissions, copyright, preprints, working papers, interviews, lectures, manuscript collections, and private documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined at 14.146; copyright issues and permissions: 4.26, 4.48, 4.81; preprints: 1.113, 14.173; source citation handling for articles not accepted, dissertations, theses, presentations, interviews, manuscript collections, and private documents: 14.146–218; working papers: 14.218; titles and file formats: 14.215, 14.225.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transliteration and transliterated text
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for transliterating non‑Latin alphabets, handling special characters, Unicode usage, transliteration resources, and treatment of titles and proper names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance in 11.71–11.76 and tables 11.2–11.5: Unicode requirements (11.2, 11.72–73, 11.90, 11.110, 11.115, 11.122); resources and tables referenced; special characters and IPA (11.21–22); transliteration for specific languages (Arabic, Chinese, Greek, Hebrew, Russian, etc.). See also titling and capitalization rules for non‑English works (11.6–11.10, 14.98–99).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and translators’ credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright, crediting translators, translator’s notes, source plus translation practices, placement of translations and retranslations, and rights for translated works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copyright and subsidiary rights: 1.20, 1.29, 4.14, 4.34, 4.64; credit/credit lines and translator’s notes: 11.14, 1.45, 14.51; placement: 11.12–17; retranslation caution and edited translations: 11.15–17; titles of works and translator credit in citations: 11.9–11.10, 14.99, 14.103–104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translators’ names in citations and title pages
rubrics_metrics.description: How to list, abbreviate, or omit the translator designation in citations and on title pages, and how to treat translators vs authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On title page: 1.19; in source citations: 14.20–21, 14.103–04, 15.6, 15.15; omission or substitution rules (e.g., translator in place of author) in text citations: 15.7, 15.22, 15.36; shortened citations: 14.32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of measurement (SI and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations, symbols, spacing, plurals, prefixes, derived units, non‑SI accepted units, place in tables, and use in text and numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance in 10.49–10.68 and 9.16–17: SI base units (10.54), derived units (10.57, 10.60), accepted non‑SI units (10.59), spacing and symbols (6.119–121, 10.52–58), plurals rules (10.65–67), and presentation in tables (3.56, fig. 3.12). See also numbers with units and table notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates, times, chronology, and time zones
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting of dates and times (spelled out vs numerals), time of day handling (noon/midnight, 24‑hour), chronology systems, eras, centuries, decades, time zones, inclusive years, and period names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: chronology systems 9.34, 9.64, 10.38; time of day abbreviations and 24‑hour system: 10.41, 9.39–9.40; time zones: 8.90, 10.41, 14.191; periods/eras/centuries/decades spelled and formatted in 7.8, 7.87–7.89, 8.71–8.74, 9.32–9.37; inclusive years and en dash rules: 9.60, 9.64, 6.78.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation and word division
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for word division and hyphenation (basic rules, prefixes/suffixes, compound terms, two‑letter endings, non‑English words), interaction with URLs/DOIs, and proofreading for bad breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word division rules: 7.36–7.47 (basic rules 7.36, pronunciation basis 7.38); compound terms and prefixes: 7.40–7.42; two‑letter endings and dips: 7.37–7.39; non‑English specifics: 11.xx references (French, German, Russian, Spanish, etc.); URLs and DOIs: 2.13, 6.113, 7.46, 14.18; proofreading for bad breaks: 2.112; typographic considerations: 7.47.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic considerations (typefaces, styles, sizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and use of typefaces, type sizes for different elements (appendixes, bibliographies, block quotations, endnotes, indexes, subheads, titles), small caps vs full capitals, spacing, and ornamentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See typographic considerations and type size sections: type size guidance for specific elements (appendixes 1.59; bibliographies 1.63; block quotations 2.19; endnotes 1.62; indexes, 1.65, 16.135; subheads 1.56, 2.59; title and subtitle 1.19); small caps and spacing issues: 10.8, 10.38, 10.5; other typographic items: captions 3.9–3.30, charts/graphs 3.42, tables 3.49–3.86.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typesetters and typesetting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions to typesetters, definition of typesetter, errors assigned to typesetters, and their role in checking/adjusting tables and mathematical copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition and responsibilities: p.989; instructions and marking for typesetters: 2.74, 2.81, 2.93, 2.116, 2.118, 2.121; errors assigned and proofreading checks: 2.135; adjusting/checking tables checklist: 3.86; see also musical examples 3.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation and submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting and submission requirements for manuscripts: manuscript formatting styles, running heads, pagination, title page conventions, word count, markup and file formats, and submission procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript prep guidance: 2.3, 2.7–2.21 (styles 2.18, 2.82–84), title page rules 1.17–1.19, running heads 1.11–1.15, pagination 1.4–1.8; word count for submission: 2.4, 2.52; markup and file formats including XML/HTML/XSL and metadata: 1.117–1.123, 2.81–2.83; digital artwork and figure submission: 3.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking changes (redlining) and version control
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions for tracking changes in author review, when to use or remove redlining, document comparison software, version numbers, and archival practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracking changes defined and conventions: p.986, 2.84; author’s review of copyedited manuscript: 2.71, 2.88; removed before submission of manuscript: 2.39; when not to use: 2.79, 2.85; document comparison software: 2.86; version control and archival practices: 1.114; version numbers: 1.28.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word processing software usage for editing and production
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended use of word processors for author review, global changes, hyphenation, styles, search & replace, macros, comment and note functions, equation editing, and Unicode/special characters support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions and uses: 2.63, 2.69–2.71, 2.79–2.88; hyphenation and line break handling: 2.13, 2.80, 7.36; styles and templates: 2.18, 2.82–84; commenting and document comparison: 2.39, 2.84, 2.86; macros and pattern matching: 2.79–80; Unicode and special character support: 11.2, 2.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and production checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreading tasks and checklists for title pages, pagination, indexes, tables, figures, captions, front matter, running heads, and typographic details; assigning proofreading responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofreading references: title page proofreading 2.134, 2.108; proofing for bad breaks and hyphenation 2.112; typesetting and pagination checks 2.103–115; cross‑checking of URLs and metadata: 2.3, 2.32–34; production checklist items: 2.77, fig. references across chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and indexing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Alphabetizing (word‑by‑word), treatment of articles at beginning of titles, indexing persons and titles, handling of non‑English forms, and index proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing guidance: alphabetizing and word‑by‑word methods 16.51–16.61, 16.104; articles at beginning of titles 8.169–170, 16.48–49; indexing of named persons, sovereigns, and religious figures: 16.37, 16.39, 16.66, 16.98, 16.134; proofing indexes 16.117, 16.131–135; resources and examples listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style/word usage and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on word usage, problematic words and phrases, consistency across text, dialect/jargon, bias‑free language and style lists; when to follow usage vs grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word usage topics: 5.249–5.250 (problematic words list and style guides); consistency emphasized (5.14); jargon and dialect considerations (5.25, 5.95, 5.174); myths and misunderstandings and guidance on acceptable/common usage (5.171, 5.180, 5.203); bias‑free/gender neutrality notes (e.g., who/whom and gender-neutral pronouns 5.255).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia and nonprint media citations
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cite and format source entries for audiovisual and multimedia items (video recordings, video games, recordings, clips, multimedia supplementary data) and their numbering/format specifics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia citation guidance: video games and multimedia content: 8.190, 14.86, 14.261–268; video recordings and clips: 1.107, 1.114, 3.10, 14.265; music and recordings: 8.193–197, 14.256; supplementary multimedia data citation: 14.112, 14.187; numbering of clips and files: 3.10.
